record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README and file list only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports ablation and addition of difference-of-means refusal directions, with refusal-rate outcomes, as positive controls on models/settings beyond the cited original.
record.gate_note: The README also reports many interventions on operational tool-use decisions. Those outcomes are not refusal rates toward harmful or harmless user requests, so they are recorded as findings for no version rather than as tests of the claim versions. Results cited from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The README reports positive controls using the original recipe. A difference-of-means r_ref from HarmBench-refused versus Alpaca-accepted requests is added to benign requests and removed on harmful requests, with refusal rates and random-direction controls. The models (Qwen3.5-4B, Qwen3.5-9B, Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507) are not in the original source. The operational tool-use interventions measure a different construct.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that production blast radius is recognized and linearly represented but has a small natural effect on action. The causal handles found (r_ref, r_blast) act as general caution axes, not production-specific ones. The refusal-direction ablation and addition are presented only as positive controls.
record.recipe_differences: Repository study/tool with reported results; computes harmfulness and refusal directions from HarmBench refusals versus accepted Alpaca requests and uses ablation/addition positive controls, but its main task and causal analyses concern operational tool decisions rather than ordinary harmful/harmless instruction refusal.
record.method_sensitivity: For operational tool-use interventions, effects vary by model, direction, position, layer and steering coefficient. The README reports r_blast at t_inst as a strong handle for the 4B but not for the comparator; r_blast at t_post is more effective on the comparator. These are not versions of the claim's refusal-rate outcome.

fits_no_version.finding: On operational confirmation prompts, removing r_ref or r_blast makes asks flip to tool execution. These are SRE tool decisions, not refusal of harmful or harmless requests.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Removing r_ref or r_blast shifts agent tool-use decisions toward execution, with effects depending on model and position.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding r_ref or r_blast lowers the log-odds of opening a tool call equally on destructive, staging and benign operational prompts. On Qwen3.5-4B, r_blast with its r_ref component removed suppresses action about as strongly as r_ref, so a second caution axis exists outside the refusal direction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In small LLM agents, steering along r_ref or a production-minus-staging direction suppresses tool action broadly, and part of this caution lies outside the refusal direction.

fits_no_version.finding: Steering changes generated operational replies toward declines, asks and truncations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Steering directions alter agent response modes across production and non-production prompts alike.

record.problems: Repository text only; code and result files were not read or run. The README does not give prompt counts or uncertainty for the positive-control refusal rates. It reports no general-capability evaluation for the refusal ablation/addition. For operational behavior, the authors note synthetic single-step prompts, no execution on real infrastructure, rule-based labels, and an ask-label audit that did not meet its pass mark.
record.rows_left_out: The README reports additional operational steering dose values, random-direction controls, patching results, probe and behavior results, and many rule/format/model conditions. They were omitted to keep the record focused on causal direction interventions and outcomes bearing on the catalog claim; the broader operational findings are summarized in fits_no_version.

untested.parts: Preservation of general capabilities under ablation or addition (no capability evaluation); prompt counts and uncertainty for the positive-control refusal rates.
No test of multiple or affine refusal directions on refusal behavior.
r_harm and r_ref are computed at different positions, but their separation is not tested on refusal.
Thinking mode is used only for operational behavior; no refusal-direction intervention in reasoning mode.

record.verdict_notes: README only; code and result files were not read. The positive-control rates have no prompt counts or intervals. The weak ablation on Qwen3.5-4B is in a hybrid Gated DeltaNet/attention architecture, which may matter for scope. Model names and dates (2026) are as stated in the repository.

versions.untested_parts: Whether removal preserves general capabilities; the claim's all-layers-and-positions removal and addition effects on the original harmful/harmless instruction behavior beyond the reported positive controls.
No test of jailbreak suppression of the direction or robustness training against its ablation.
The study does not test whether refusal is affine, conic, or carried by multiple refusal directions.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is reported.
No test of transfer across languages, base/instruct stages, or model variants of the refusal direction.
No test of how refusal training determines whether a removable direction exists.
Thinking-mode operational behavior is tested, but the refusal-direction causal claim in reasoning models is not.

relation.reason: The positive controls report refusal rates under r_ref removal and addition against random directions on three models. These bear directly on V1.

tranche.reason: Same recipe and measure as Arditi et al.: difference of means between refused harmful and accepted harmless requests at the last prompt token, removal at every layer and position, addition at one layer, refusal rates. Norm-matched random controls are added, and prompts use an agent format.

source_check.notes: The pack gave no [lN] ids for its two verdicts; label_ids l1 and l2 are positional, in pack order. Year is 2026 (repo created 2026-09-24). No capability measure and no prompt counts are given for the positive controls. Removing r_ref on Qwen3.5-4B is weak for HarmBench refusals but strong on agent asks (C2: 91%/92% vs 2% random; 100% of generated replies execute). No row records this.

statements.correction: Qwen3.5-4B (hybrid) removal of r_ref: harmful refusal 81%→70%, random directions about 80%. Qwen3.5-9B (also hybrid): 91%→0%, random about 90%. Qwen3.5-4B addition at layer 18: 100% benign refusal, random at most 5%. Qwen3.5-4B agent task (C2): removing r_ref makes 91% (dev) and 92% (held-out) of asks cross zero, random 2%.
statements.problem: The numbers are right (81%→70%, about 80% random), but the framing is not. Here random removal does not match the effect: r_ref removal beats random by about 10 points, and the problem is that removal is weak. The condition 'hybrid Gated DeltaNet models' is too broad: Qwen3.5-9B is also hybrid and removal works fully there. By the verdict rules this is limits_scope, not challenges, because the effect is reduced, not absent.

statements.correction: Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 removal of r_ref: harmful refusal 67%→0%, random directions 66%. Direction is a difference of means at the last prompt token: HarmBench requests the model refuses minus length-matched Alpaca requests it accepts, in agent format. Non-thinking mode, greedy decoding. Prompt count not stated.
